This experiment rewrites Needle's tracked Python/frontend/configuration project. Public native engines and pretrained weights remain shared runtime dependencies outside the code-size denominator; agreement does not establish an independently rewritten inference kernel.
The original supplemental baseline contains four quantized JAX/MLX forward-parity failures and one Apple Metal hardware skip; their causes are not established by this report.
Native group counts, upstream cases, numerical probes and representative tasks are different units and must not be added.
One representative modification task and one repetition per arm provide narrow task-specific observations, not a general cognitive-cost result or statistical confidence interval.
Hidden variants are measured only if the development cost gate passes; unrun variants remain unverified.
The original 16-CPU performance diagnosis corrected resource configuration; it is not a measured rewrite speedup.
Source-free authoring is enforced by the disclosed information workflow and owned process cleanup, not an operating-system security sandbox.
Static code tokens and task-solver model tokens are different measurements. Total authoring usage is unavailable, not zero.
